ffmpeg.setup_linux:
Setup (either way):
  - Install it with the system: sudo apt install ffmpeg (Debian, Ubuntu) or sudo dnf install ffmpeg-free (Fedora).
    The program finds it by itself.
  - Or download a static FFmpeg build for Linux and copy it into a folder named 'ffmpeg' beside the program, so that the 'bin'
    folder (with the ffmpeg and ffprobe programs) is at ffmpeg/bin. A build there is used before the one of the system.
Then choose "Look for FFmpeg again" below.
ffmpeg.setup_windows:
Setup:
  1. Download a Windows FFmpeg build.
  2. Copy it into a folder named 'ffmpeg' beside the program, so that the 'bin' folder
     (with the FFmpeg and FFprobe programs) is at ffmpeg\bin.
  3. Choose "Look for FFmpeg again" below.

preset.explain:
The Jellyfin default is what Jellyfin makes itself.
It replaces the image settings only; key frames and the rules
for existing outputs stay as they are.
image.intro: How the thumbnails look: their size and how often one is taken.
image.width_explain: Width of one thumbnail in pixels (Jellyfin: 320).
image.interval_explain: How often a thumbnail is taken, in seconds (Jellyfin: 10).
image.columns_explain: How many thumbnails sit in a row of one tile sheet (Jellyfin: 10).
image.rows_explain: How many rows of thumbnails one tile sheet has (Jellyfin: 10).
image.qscale_explain: JPEG quality while FFmpeg extracts the thumbnails: 1 is best, 31 is worst (Jellyfin: 4).
image.quality_explain: JPEG quality of the finished tile sheet, 1 to 100 (Jellyfin: 90).
keyframes.intro: Extraction is faster when the decoder only decodes key frames.
keyframes.only_explain1:
The decoder skips every picture that is not a key frame,
which can make big files much faster.
keyframes.only_explain2:
A thumbnail then comes from the nearest key frame before its time.
If that way fails for a file, all frames are decoded.
keyframes.switch_explain:
Where the key frames of a file are further apart than the interval, thumbnails repeat.
A video with a larger share of repeated thumbnails is extracted again with every frame (0 = never).

disks.title: Disks
disks.explain:
Videos on the same physical disk are processed one after the other
(or as many at a time as you set); different disks work at the same time.
disks.pick_drive: Every drive letter or share is its own disk
disks.pick_manual: I will group the media folders myself
disks.assign: Give each media folder the name of a disk group.
disks.per_disk_explain: How many videos are processed at once on the same disk. A hard disk reads one video well and two badly (the heads jump between the files); an SSD copes with two.
disks.pick_workers_auto: Automatic: {hdd} on an HDD, {ssd} on an SSD [recommended]
disks.pick_workers_number: The same number on every disk
disks.intro: How many videos are processed at once.
fingerprint.intro:
How a changed video is noticed: by its size and date,
or also by reading a few bytes from its start and end (slower, surer).
fingerprint.now: Also read the start and end of each video: {value}
maintenance.not_touched: The state database and the configuration are not touched.

maintenance.reset_explain:
The program forgets what it processed before,
as if you had just unpacked it.
The next scan finds and checks the existing trickplay again.
maintenance.reset_not_touched: Not touched: trickplay images, media files, configuration.

maintenance.forget_explain:
The program forgets which FFmpeg builds it knows and what it
checked about them. FFmpeg folders are not deleted.

hdr_review.heading: HDR REVIEW
hdr_review.explain:
Compare brightness and colors of every kind of HDR and GPU backend with the source in your usual player.
The CPU is also under review: it is not automatically a correct color reference.
Pictures: "... - all paths.jpg" of each kind of HDR shows CPU and every GPU backend side by side, a row per segment.
Details (CPU vs GPU per segment) are in comparisons\, single frames in samples\.

video and whether key frames pay off (often 2 to 3 times faster).
